source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed electrical appliance safety checks

1. Start with the test records.
2.
completion:
Record the date and time of the safety check.
3. Indicate the make and model of the appliance.
4. Identity the serial number or unique identifier of the appliance.
5. List the specific safety checks performed and their outcomes (pass/fail).
6. Document the nature of the failure(s) in detail.
7. Include the test equipment used, including its calibration status.
8. Note the name and qualifications of the person who conducted the test.
9. Attach any relevant photographs or diagrams showing faults or defects.
10. Specify any corrective measures advised or undertaken.
11. Cross-reference with any maintenance records or previous checks.
12. Log the safety check results in a central database or register.
13. Record recommendations for remedial action and further checks.
14. Keep copies of all documentation for at least the required retention period.
15. Ensure that the documentation is sequentially numbered or indexed for audit purposes.
16. After documenting, store the failed appliance
